hed.text: Two ways to open the About page

a.text:
A — THE MARK, LIT.

The Gila is the hero: deep ground, two light sources, the mark glowing. Dramatic, unmistakably yours, and it reads at any size.

Strength: nobody else in this category looks like this. It is the badass option.

Risk: it is a beautifully lit logo rather than a scene. If the rest of the site stays pale blue, this one dark panel can feel bolted on unless the dark band repeats elsewhere — the footer already is dark, so it has somewhere to rhyme with.

b.text:
B — PHOTOGRAPHIC, CALM.

The hand shot you made carries the page. The mark appears small, as a signature rather than a billboard. Closer to the calm you liked about Nurish.

Strength: real texture, real light, and a human holding the actual product. It is warmer and more premium.

Risk: the photo's background is beige, so it sits slightly apart from the blue page. It also leans on photography being good — and the vial in this shot still carries the old cap and the old lizard, so it needs re-rendering before it ships.

note.text: Both use the same words — the About copy built around the Gila, with "Anyone can fill a vial" kept and the provenance line that stops the history reading as a claim. So you are judging the look, not the writing.
